label: D2: chose a2 and reached S2 (common) after an unrewarded previous trial
explanation: Fires only at D2 (never at D1 or GO). Active when the agent chose a2 and landed in S2 via the common transition, and the previous trial was unrewarded (reward input 0 at this trial D1). All variables are observed at D2. Dev: P 0.99, R 0.97, F1 0.98, mass recall 0.99. Dropping the prev_reward condition gives F1 0.54 (it is silent on a2->S2 after a rewarded trial). Dropping the action condition gives F1 0.87, so a1->S2 (rare) barely drives it. Does not fire on S1 or on a1. The misses are concentrated in the lowest activation quartile. I did not test what modulates magnitude beyond this.

issues: Every factual claim held up on test. The unit has 0 active steps at D1 and GO and puts 100% of its activation mass at D2. Dropping prev_reward gives F1 0.550 (precision 0.38), and dropping the action condition gives F1 0.870 (precision 0.78). Both match the reported 0.54 and 0.87.

The test misses split into two small groups. The first is a2 reaching S2 after a rewarded trial (predicate with prev_reward==1: precision 0.013, recall 0.021). The second is a1 reaching S2 by a rare transition (in_action==1 predicate: recall 0.007). Both are weak, low-magnitude activations; the missed steps hold only 0.8% of activation mass. False positives look scattered, with no visible pattern by trial position or good state.
One minor wording point: '(common)' in the label adds nothing, because a2 reaching S2 is the common transition by definition. Also, magnitude modulation was not examined.
No future variables are used: action, state and previous reward are all observed by D2.
